tweets.text:
Solana 4.2 + V1 is coming to the stack. 👀🚀  Stay tuned!

Shipstern now handles V1 without changing the Legacy/V0 paths.

Legacy → unchanged
V0     → unchanged + ALT
V1     → config preserved
Message.config was the easiest thing to accidentally lose.
Devnet V1 txs now go through Jetstreamer’s wincode decode path, including txs >1232 bytes.

Thanks to @Sam0xSol  and @espicodes

quotedTweet.text:
Shipstern 0.9.0 is out.

Live filter updates on the Yellowstone gRPC source. Take a RuntimeHandle, patch the filter set with update_filters, the subscription is replaced mid-stream. No reconnect.

Also: Transaction V1 (SIMD-0385) support with the inline compute budget on InstructionShared, Prefilter now covers the full Yellowstone subscription surface (memcmp, datasize, lamports, data slices, accounts_exclude, vote, interslot_updates), DISCRIMINATOR constants on generated types, and CPI event envelopes read straight from the IDL.

Breaking if you match exhaustively on PrefilterError or build prefilters with struct literals. Builder users unaffected.

https://github.com/solana-rpc/shipstern/releases/tag/v0.9.0

tweets.text:
Host tools are dropped from i686-pc-windows-msvc, implementing RFC 3999.

That landed as an auto merge in rust-lang/rust, along with collapsing two test jobs into one. Elsewhere in the tree, a rollup stops explicitly specifying OnDuplicate::Error since it's the default.

A second rollup minimizes DiagCtxt methods. The commit establishes a clearer rule: methods should not go on DiagCtxt, splitting placement between DiagCtxt, DiagCtxtInner, and DiagCtxtHandle.

Closures just became MaybeDangling in Rust, and that's a bigger aliasing-model deal than it sounds. The change extends to coroutines and coroutine closures, aligning them with the aliasing model's expectations.

Meanwhile, libc deprecates the POSIX-obsoleted tmpnam and tempnam. Both are TOCTOU-prone, tmpnam isn't thread-safe with NULL, and glibc docs reportedly say never use tempnam. The writing was on the wall.

Miri's TCP socket implementation now manually sets initial readiness flags for new sockets, covering read-closed, write-closed, and writable states, until an underlying host socket exists.
